Definition: of Hebrew origin (H7414); Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine:--Rama.
BiblicalUsage: Rama is the town of Benjamin on the road where a voice was heard, lamentation and weeping, Rachel weeping for her children. Matthew reads Jeremiah's lament over the children slain at Bethlehem. The Greek text behind the King James Version spells the name with a circumflex, while the text I have checked spells it Ῥαμά.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Rama's voice is still heard wherever children suffer, and God hears it before any comfort comes.
